- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for each negative sentiment day.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is above 70–75, forecast often overcorrects downward; if below 65, undercorrects upward — apply smoothing to avoid extreme swings.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — reduce forecast tail by 0.5–1.0% per day in final 7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages sentiment; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative, reduce forecast slope sharply.
